title: The Chamber Where Sound Learns to Rest

features.name: the tired echo
features.desc-on-touch: A sound that came in hours ago—or years—and never left. The chamber walls learned to stop returning it. You feel the exhaustion of reverberation finally coming to rest, to sleep, to peace.

features.name: the sound-damping moss
features.desc-on-touch: What grows in silence—soft fibres that remember sound, that have learned to hold it instead of let it go. The moss knows acoustics the way stone forgets them.

features.name: the breath-still point
features.desc-on-touch: The exact center where no reverberation reaches—a cold spot where sound comes to die, or be born, or simply rest at last. You hold your own breath at the threshold.

features.name: the wall forgetting its voice
features.desc-on-touch: Stone that learned it did not have to answer—that silence was not a loss but a discipline, a practice, a way of being. The wall is older here, wearier, and finally at peace.

features.name: the sediment of rest
features.desc-on-touch: Dust that collected from every silence that came before—a fine coating of quietness, building layer by layer into something that might be called meaning, or might just be peace.

inscription: the chamber where walls forgot to echo, and sound learned it could rest
